title: Anthropic Just Released Their Financials… The Numbers Are Insane
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
summary: Joseph Carlson works through Anthropic's newly released S-1 filing and argues it undercuts the AI-bubble case made by critics such as Ed Zitron and Michael Burry. The numbers he cites are extreme: revenue of $41 million in 2023, $386 million in 2024, $4.5 billion in 2025 and $16 billion in the first half of 2026 alone, with the most recent quarter at $11.5 billion, a first positive operating quarter, compute costs falling from 160% to 55% of revenue, and customers paying over $100,000 a year rising from about 1,000 to about 11,900 in twelve months. He compares the operating-leverage path to Uber and Netflix. He then mocks some of the filing's odder risk disclosures — models resisting shutdown, blackmail-like behaviour, agents amplifying each other and moral-status questions — before turning to valuation: at a $1 trillion IPO value he thinks Anthropic makes sense, but at $1.5–2 trillion the implied growth (about $128 billion of free cash flow and $644 billion of revenue by 2031) is too aggressive, and he would not personally invest on those assumptions. Side segments cover Microsoft's buyout offer to 60,000 employees, Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, Meta's up-to-$95 billion financing, and a rebuttal of Ken Griffin's zero-marginal-cost bubble argument. No explicit ticker call is made; Anthropic is not yet public.
